A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FS-KAN work. Their main sections, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E can be matched and read reliably. The formatting changes and additional appendix results do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original symbolic-function learning, signal classification, ModelNet40 classification and continual learning, rating prediction, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds full-training-set ModelNet40 results and further runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The function-sharing construction, invariant/equivariant layers and efficient aggregation variant remain unchanged. The added explanation of efficient layers for arbitrary groups restates the construction already provided in v1 Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same symbolic tasks, synthetic signals, ModelNet40 classification and corruption scenario, and four rating datasets. The added full-training-set ModelNet40 experiment changes sample count within existing coverage, without introducing a new task or population.

E2.justification: Tables 4–5 add Point-Transformer and standard KAN to the runtime and memory comparisons, which previously contained only DeepSets and the two FS-KAN variants. These comparators already appeared in v1's classification-accuracy comparison; the other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 adds evaluation with 8,859 ModelNet40 training samples and 1,024 points per cloud. Appendix D adds resource measurements across the retained architectural grid. Existing splits, preprocessing, model configurations and hyperparameter-search settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D substantially extends the accuracy-based architectural study into an accuracy–cost analysis, measuring training/inference time and peak memory across depth, width and spline-grid choices in new Tables 8–11. Tables 4–5 also broaden resource-scaling comparisons. The interpretability and continual-learning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting. Table 4 retains runtime measurement over ten steps. Additional accuracy and timing entries follow existing reporting practices; no changed run counts or new statistical procedures are documented.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports full-data accuracies of 0.837±0.007 for FS-KAN, 0.840±0.005 for efficient FS-KAN, 0.844±0.005 for DeepSets, 0.840±0.008 for Point-Transformer and 0.232±0.074 for standard KAN. Expanded Tables 4–5 and new Tables 8–11 substantially extend resource results. Earlier benchmark figures, Table 1 and architectural accuracies remain unchanged; the latter move from v1 Table 6 to v2 Table 7.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–8, Corollary 4.1 and the derivations and proofs in Appendices A–B retain their mathematical substance. The added explanation of spline degree/grid notation and the f_epsilon notation in Proposition 7 do not change assumptions or guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims about arbitrary permutation symmetries, expressive-power equivalence, low-data efficiency, interpretability and adaptability. The additional experiments support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds the interpretation that full-data accuracy is comparable to established baselines. Appendix D changes the recommended configuration from depth 4/width 64 to depth 4/width 128/grid 4, revises the stated width-related gain from approximately 0.005–0.010 to 0.010–0.015, and adds cost-scaling and diminishing-return interpretations despite retaining the accuracy table.

D1.justification: The expanded timing and GPU-memory tables provide additional practical resource information for existing baselines and architectural choices. Software, optimizers, V100 hardware, implementation sources and previously documented hyperparameters remain unchanged; no new code or data access provision is stated.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to equivariant networks and earlier KAN approaches are retained. Citation formatting and expanded author names in the bibliography do not introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief explanations of the star operator, general-group efficient aggregation, uniform approximation and spline notation, and rewrites the Appendix D interpretation. It updates publication headers and citation style while retaining the section sequence and most prose.

P2.justification: The ICLR format changes text width, title/header styling, display sizes and figure/table placement throughout. Tables 4–5 gain rows, and five new tables present full-data accuracy and architectural resource profiles. All eight figure images are retained, but Figures 1–2 acquire unresolved '??' subfigure references.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the full-data ModelNet40 comparison and broader resource measurements make accuracy and computational tradeoffs better supported. The gain is limited by broken subfigure references and insufficient justification for the revised 'optimal' configuration: at depth 4/grid 4, width 128 improves mean accuracy over width 64 by only 0.005 while roughly doubling training time and memory.
